title: Book Three · Chapter 132: The Largest Cup
story:
In the fourth week, Ronan uses his question sheet at the counter.

Mr Sun looked at it on Monday. He added one line for the next step and left the short questions in place.

On Wednesday, the woman with the cups comes back. This time, her shelf is finished.

Mr Sun brings it to the front. She has brought the largest cup again to try the space.

It fits. The handle stays clear of the edge.

The woman smiles and turns the cup around.

“The others are all smaller.”

She lifts it once, then puts it near the other end of the shelf.

“Here, I think.”

Ronan looks at the clear wood beside it. He has spent weeks thinking about the biggest cup. She is thinking about all the cups in her own kitchen.

“Is that its usual place?” he asks.

“It will be. I use the small ones first.”

She takes hold of the handle and lifts the cup toward herself. Her fingers have room beside the wood.

Mr Sun waits while she tries from the other side too.

Ronan finds her first drawing among the papers. The little circles are still there, with one much larger than the rest.

The woman laughs when he puts it beside the shelf.

“It looks like a pot there.”

“Only on paper.”

She gives him a smile and picks up her real cup. Ronan leaves the drawing with the checked papers while Mr Sun looks at the finished edge again.

“Even with their handles?” Ronan asks.

She laughs. “Even then.”

Mr Sun checks the shelf with her and takes her payment. He gives her the receipt while Ronan finds the wrapping paper.

She puts her cup back in her bag. Mr Sun wraps the shelf, and she lifts it from the counter with both hands.

Ronan opens the door. He waits while she takes the first step, then moves back inside.

There is already another customer at the table. He wants a wooden stand for a sign outside his tea stall.

Ronan finds a clean sheet. He starts with the name and asks about the place.

“Near the door,” the man says.

“How much room is there?”

The man shows him with his hands. Then he draws the door and the step.

Ronan looks at the narrow space.

“Does the sign have to go inside at night?”

“Every night.”

He adds that below the drawing. The man explains the place behind the door where he will keep it.

Mr Sun comes over to read. Ronan tells him about the outside space and the move indoors.

Mr Sun asks the man for the inside space too. They arrange the next measurement together.

After the customer leaves, Dad looks at the drawing beside Ronan.

“A sign with two homes.”

“And a very narrow front door.”

Dad studies the step and points out another place to check. Ronan writes the question in the open space at the bottom.

They carry the sheet to Mr Sun together.

At the short break, Ronan sits near the workshop door. His shirt is warm against his back, and he drinks the last of his water.

Dad comes to refill his cup. He rests his hands on the counter while the water pours.

“Better today?” Ronan asks.

“Better with the breaks.”

Dad lifts his cup and returns to the other worker. Ronan stays on the bench for a few more minutes. Then he folds his question sheet and goes back to the front table.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

receipt＝收据；stand＝支架、展示架；indoors＝在室内、往室内；refill＝重新装满。

## 理解问题

1. 最大的杯子和架子怎样实际完成核对与取走？付款由谁接收？
2. Ronan问了招牌支架的哪个使用问题？为什么还要知道室内空间？

## 读句子

**The handle stays clear of the edge.**

拆开看：The handle / stays clear / of the edge.

杯把／没有挨着／架子边缘。
